subject: Keystore wrapping & log-sampling triage — scope for SSO/session-correlation evidence
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Julie Barnes <julie.barnes@novamed.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Keystore wrapping & log-sampling triage — scope for SSO/session-correlation evidence

Team / Julie,

Following MedSprint's audit request (see attached evidence checklist), we need to triage three related asks that are overlapping but distinct: keystore wrapping for per-tenant CMKs, sampled audit logs for short retention windows, and SSO/session correlation IDs for forensic timelines. I want us to align on owners and minimal deliverables so we can commit to a timeline for MedSprint's compliance window.

High level proposal (short):
- Engineering (Rishi + Priyom): validate feasibility of per-tenant key wrapping using existing KMS envelope patterns and estimate effort for short-lived wrapped keys (30d rolling).
- Product (Marissa): confirm whether we can accept a sampled log package (vs full exports) for the MedSprint SLA and define sampling granularity (per-tenant, per-route).
- Security/Compliance (Kimberly): review evidence template and confirm which artifacts are acceptable for the auditor.
- Customer (Julie / AuditOps): confirm the acceptance criteria and any mandatory fields (e.g., session-id, user-hash, tenant-id) that must be present in logs.

Notes / constraints I want flagged early:
- We must avoid long-lived plaintext keys in our control plane for Private deployments.
- Sampling must still preserve the ability to reconstruct a user session in the event of an incident (i.e., ordered events with correlation id).
- Any exported evidence must not leak PII — plan for redaction or hashing in the package.

Next steps: can everyone reply with one-line ownership + the most important blocker by EOD Monday? Julie, if you can list the top 3 fields your auditors require, that will help narrow the scope.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: keystore-wrapping-proposal.pdf (4 pages, design notes), log-sampling-matrix.csv (matrix of sampling options), evidence-pack-template.docx (package checklist)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Keystore wrapping & log-sampling triage — scope for SSO/session-correlation evidence

Vivek / team —

Ownership: Product owner for the feature: Marissa (I will own scope + customer acceptance).

Primary product asks / constraints from PMs:
- Sampling model: product is comfortable with a "tiered sampling" approach: 100% for admin-level ops, 10% for normal traffic, and adaptive spike capture (auto-escalate to 100% for 15 minutes when anomaly detected). We need a quick-proof that we can reconstruct session order under that model.
- Keystore UX: customers with Private or Dedicated should be able to bring their own CMK (wrapped) or let Redwood provision with an opt-in wrapped-rotation policy. Must avoid requests that require manual rotation steps for customers in 90%+ of flows.
- Delivery: minimum viable evidence package = ordered events + correlation id + redacted user identifier. Full raw logs can be produced but behind additional privacy gating and CS coordination.

Blockers I see now:
1) Runtime bookkeeping for sampled logs (ordering, sequence IDs) will add ~2 infra weeks to the pipeline unless we can piggyback on existing courier stream.
2) Keystore wrapping with customer-managed import will require changes to onboarding flow and CAI (customer acceptance) checks — legal needs to weigh in on terms if customers manage their own keys.

I can prod CS/legal for quick guidance. Rishi / Priyom — estimates?

- Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
VP, Product 
Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek / Marissa — quick clarifications from the auditor side to keep this pragmatic: 
Top 3 fields our auditors will insist on in the exported package:
1) session_correlation_id (consistent across front-end request and downstream service logs)
2) tenant_id (our multi-tenant mapping)
3) event_timestamp (ISO8601 with timezone)

Additional asks:
- A short writeup on how keys are wrapped/rotated and who holds the envelope keys (for Private deploys the auditor wants a description and a timeline of rotations).
- Proof that sampled exports preserve ordering for at least 99% of sessions that include admin actions.

We are ok with a sampled export as long as the above are satisfied and we get a short runbook on how to request a full export under exceptional circumstances (incident + legal).

Julie Barnes

Subject: Re: Keystore wrapping & log-sampling triage — scope for SSO/session-correlation evidence

Thanks — ownership acknowledged (Rishi / Priyom for infra work). Quick technical notes and immediate blockers: 

Technical approach proposals:
- Keystore wrapping: use per-tenant envelope keys stored in our HSM-backed KMS; for Private we will support importing a wrapped CMK (customer provides an RSA-wrapped blob we unwrap and store encrypted) — avoids storing plaintext. We can implement a 30-day rotation window via automated rewraps. Estimate: 3 dev weeks + 1 week QA.
- Sampling/ordering: retain a lightweight sequence vector per-session (append-only event counter) persisted to the stream. If we piggyback on existing event-stream offsets, we can reduce effort to ~7 engineering days.
- Redaction: we will hash user identifiers with a per-tenant salt (kept encrypted) before export; auditors can request salt disclosures under legal process.

Immediate blockers:
1) Legal needs to confirm whether hashed identifiers are acceptable as evidence without salts.
2) Dedicated/private onboarding flow must be modified — product + legal alignment required.

Proposed immediate deliverables (MVP for MedSprint):
- Design doc PR with schema and sequence approach (by Sep 6)
- Small POC that produces an evidence package (sampled) with session ordering preserved (by Sep 20)

I'll create the INF ticket and link design docs. Priyom / Kim — can you own the infra spike and compliance review respectively?

Rishi
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime
